add.title: 🔧 Why the list is 3× too long (the system fix)
add.text:
Three ways one question shows up several times:

1. **A plan handed down waits twice:** once on the agent that wrote it, once on the agent that handed it down (items 1 and 2, 4 and 5, 6 and 16).
2. **An agent's whole session shows as waiting** whenever one of its tasks waits (items 16, 17, 19, 20).
3. **One task is listed twice:** at its own folder and again at its parent's folder (items 9–11 repeat 12–14).

And one wait outlives its answer: a merge step still "waits" 17 days after its work landed (items 7, 8).

The fix belongs in the "waiting" list's code, not in closing items by hand: count a wait once, at the task that holds it.

why.title: 🔧 Why the list is so long (the system fixes)
why.text:
Five ways one question, or no question, ends up "waiting on you":

1. **A plan handed down waits twice:** once on the agent that wrote it, once on the agent that handed it down (items 1 and 2, 4 and 5, 6 and 16).
2. **An agent's whole session shows as waiting** whenever one of its tasks waits (items 16, 17, 19, 20, 33).
3. **One task is listed twice:** at its own folder and again at its parent's (items 9–11 repeat 12–14).
4. **A daily check-in re-posts a wait as a new question card** each day, so one waiting voice call shows up four times (items 21–24 and 26–29).
5. **A wait never ends when its agent does:** budget pauses from 10-17 (items 35–40), voice calls that ended on 11-03 (28, 29), merges that landed 17 days ago (7, 8).

The fix belongs in the "waiting" list's code, not in closing items by hand: count a wait once, at the task that holds it, and drop it when its agent has ended.

why.title: 🔧 Why the list is so long (the system fixes)
why.text:
Six ways one question, or no question, ends up "waiting on you":

1. **A plan handed down waits twice:** once on the agent that wrote it, once on the agent that handed it down (items 1 and 2, 4 and 5, 6 and 16).
2. **An agent's whole session shows as waiting** whenever one of its tasks waits (items 16, 17, 19, 20, 33).
3. **One task is listed twice:** at its own folder and again at its parent's (items 9–11 repeat 12–14).
4. **A daily check-in re-posts a wait as a new question card** each day, so one waiting voice call shows up four times (items 21–24 and 26–29).
5. **A wait never ends when its agent does:** budget pauses and cost gates from 10-03 to 10-17 (items 35–42 and 44–51), voice calls that ended on 11-03 (28, 29), merges that landed 17 days ago (7, 8).
6. **Any card left with an open reply box counts as a question,** even a mic check or a test card (items 43, 54), and a decision stays open after its work was built (items 55, 56).

The fix belongs in the "waiting" list's code, not in closing items by hand: count a wait once, at the task that holds it, drop it when its agent has ended, and count a card only when it asks something.
